newsitem.title: CANADA: Ag Canada sees oilseeds gain ground on grains 97/8.
newsitem.headline: Ag Canada sees oilseeds gain ground on grains 97/8.

text.p: Oilseeds and specialty crops were forecast to gain ground at the expense of wheat, barley and oats in crop year 1997/98 (Aug/July), Agriculture Canada said on Monday.
"For 1997/98, area seeded in Canada is expected to shift from wheat, barley and oats into oilseeds and specialty crops," Agriculture Canada said in its March supply and demand report.
While wheat, coarse grain and oilseed prices were expected to decline in 1997/98 on rising world output, values should remain well above the levels of the early 1990s, Ag Can said.
"Projected lower Canadian exports of durum, barley and corn are expected to be more than offset by higher exports of wheat (ex-durum), oats, canola, flax and soybeans," it said.

The condition of the 1997 U.S. winter wheat crop, the size of spring seeded crops in the major producing nations, the aggressiveness of European Union and U.S. export subsidies and China's import demands will all affect price levels, it said.

Wheat (ex-durum) output in 1997/98 should drop despite higher carry-in stocks. Exports should to rise in 1997/98 because of reduced competition from Australia and Argentina and carry-out should fall to a historic low of 6.0 million T.
"Although (durum wheat) production is forecast to equal the record of 4.7 million tonnes set last year, supplies and exports are expected to decrease," Ag Can said.
Barley export forecasts were revised down for 1996/97 on lower exports to date and may lead to more feeding and carry out stocks. Exports in 1997/98 were cut on lower supplies.
Feed barley exports should drop slightly while malt barley exports should to remain strong, Ag Can said.
"Domestic (canola) crush is forecast to be similar to the record set in 1995/96, supported by the recent improvement in the very poor crush margins," Ag Can said.

"However, tight supplies are expected to keep prices relatively strong. Given trend yields, Canadian canola production is expected to increase by over 30 percent to 7.0 million tonnes in 1997/98 as seeded area is expected to increase by 50 percent," Ag Can said.
"Domestic demand and exports are expected to increase significantly. Canola prices are expected to decline slightly, in line with other oilseeds," it added.
Flax exports in 1996/97 may not reach the forecast 700,000 tonnes unless European import demand picks up. Relatively high prices were expected to boost seeded acreage by 26 percent.
